newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Santander Investment names Vnesh Russian best debt.
newsitem.headline: Santander Investment names Vnesh Russian best debt.

text.p: Santander Investment said that Vnesh Principal loans and uninsured trade credits would be the best Russian paper over the next few months.

"We reiterate our view that Vnesh Principal loans will be among the best-performing sector of the Russian fixed-income markets over the next several months, along with uninsured trade credits," Santander said in a research note dated April 17 and obtained by Reuters on Friday.
The Vnesh loan market rose after a statement from the Russian Finance Ministry saying the London Club rescheduling would close this August, Santander said.
Previously the market had feared it might not be completed by the December 31 "drop-dead" date, when principal loans trading on a when-issued basis would become worthless.
Santander said GKO discount Treasury bills were attractive, but not as much as Vnesh. Less interesting were MinFins and Russia's outstanding Eurobonds.

Russia's debt-servicing costs are unobtrusive, less than 10 percent of export revenues for both 1996 and 1997, and net external debt remains modest at around 28 percent of gross domestic product, it said.

One concern is the unimpressive debt service cover and the slow intermediation of export receipts through the banking system to the official reserves, but with the seven-year grace periods on the restructured Vnesh loans this is not an immediate risk, it said.
